name: Plants for childbirth recovery and vaginal "cleansing" (Haitian and Caribbean women)
what_people_do: Women use food plants as teas, baths and vaginal preparations after childbirth and for gynaecological infections or "cleansing"; the practice continues after migration.
why_they_say_it_works: Plants are believed to clean the womb, heal after birth and prevent infection.

documented_by.source: Vardeman ET, Kennelly EJ, Vandebroek I 2024, J Ethnobiol Ethnomed, PMID 38217006
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Haitian women in New York: 97% used medicinal plants in Haiti and 83% after moving to the USA; childbirth and puerperium, gynaecological infections and vaginal cleansing were priority concerns; most plants were global food plants.

documented_by.source: Caribbean Women's Health and Transnational Ethnobotany 2022, Econ Bot, PMID 34522053
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Dominican surveys (DR and NYC): gynaecological infections were the top women's health condition treated with plants; authors note plants for infections could disturb the vaginal microbiota and may increase rather than prevent disease.

evidence.finding: Several species are known antibacterials but remain untested for effect on vaginal flora; authors flag a public health need to test them.

source.name: Caribbean Women's Health and Transnational Ethnobotany 2022, Econ Bot, PMID 34522053

harm_note: Authors raise the possibility of vaginal dysbiosis (hypothesised, not demonstrated in these sources).
gaps: No clinical study; which specific plants were used internally vs vaginally not extracted.
